newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper rallies to end at two-month high.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper rallies to end at two-month high.

text.p: Copper finally lifted itself from the summer lull to a two-month high, rallying higher on a mix of technical and fundamental factors with no reprieve seen in the short-term, traders and analysts said.
Shorts, particulary those in nearby months, were forced to cover aggressively. Delta LME option buying then powered prices in underlying futures through key technical barriers.

But Mike Frawley of Dean Witter said the rally was largely based on fundamentals - good physical buying in the Far East in recent days pushed up cash premiums, a sign that people believed there were no huge metal stocks in the region.

"Physical business in the States has also been excellent and the marketplace was somewhat short to begin with," Frawley said. "The market is going to remain very tight through the middle of September at the very least."
December copper settled 4.55 cents higher at 95.25 cents per lb, traded 95.70 to 90.90 cents. September was up 5.00 cents at 96.50 cents. Volume was estimated at 10,000 lots.
LME stocks rose Friday less than expected, and a strike began at Codelco's Salvador mine and concentrator. The smelter and refinery were operating near normally, the company said.
COMEX is closed Monday for Labor Day holiday.
